rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The six-day creation trains the wise in patience and deliberation toward God's servants, while the days count as a lesson to the heedless.
rows.anchor: تعجيب للغبي الجاهل , تدريب للفطن العالم في الحلم والأناة والصبر على عباد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Days began only after the sun was created; assigning six days, like all divine acts, has great wisdom even when people cannot grasp it.
rows.anchor: الأيام ما حدثت إلا بعد خلق الشمس , الإقرار بأن تخصيص هذا العدد لداعي حكمه عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made Friday a Muslim festival because creation gathered there when Adam was created in its final hour.
rows.anchor: وجعل الله الجمعة عيدا للمسلمين لأن الخلق اجتمع فيه بخلق آدم عليه السلام فيه في آخر ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing Himself over the Throne means beginning the governance of the created kingdom.
rows.anchor: أي شرع في تدبير لهذا الملك الذي اخترعه وأوجده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continuously creates every substance and attribute, including human sins, refuting those who say He now acts only through causes fixed in eternity.
rows.anchor: ولا تحدث فيه ذرة من ذات أو معنى إلا بخلق جديد منه سبحانه , ردا على من يقول من اليهود وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rahman is the one whose mercy preceded His wrath and who benefits even those who disbelieve in Him.
rows.anchor: أي الذي سبقت رحمته غضبهن وهو يحسن إلى من يكفره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers especially should embody mercy; God treats even those who insult and deny Him mercifully, unlike worldly rulers who punish disobedience despite their incapacity.
rows.anchor: فأجدر عباده بالتخلق بهذا الخلق رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asking God as the expert yields the truth of any matter at its beginning, present state, and end; the Prophet should not despair because God knows his opponents and will grant him success.
rows.anchor: عن هذه الأمور وكل أمر تريده ليخبرك بحقيقة أمره ابتداء وحالا ومآلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration means submission through prayer and other forms of humility.
rows.anchor: أي اخضعوا بالصلاة وغيرها { للرحمن } الذي لا نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers feign ignorance of the Merciful, using the interrogative for an irrational thing as though they did not know Him, let alone thank Him.
rows.anchor: متجاهلين عن معرفته فضلا عن كفر نعمته معبرين بأداة ما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi suggests their wording may indicate ignorance of God's attribute rather than ignorance of the one described.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي : إنهم إما عبروا بذلك إشارة إلى جهلهم الصفة , دون الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They repeat the irrational-form wording in rejecting the command, now directing it also against the caller who summoned them.
rows.anchor: فعبروا عنه بعد التجاهل في أمره والإنكار على الداعي إليه أيضا بأداة ما لا يعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear call to gratitude instead increased their flight because satanic heat drove them on; this is the strongest possible aversion and blame.
rows.anchor: لما عندهم من الحرارة الشيطانية التي تؤزهم أزا , فلا نفرة توازي هذه النفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The twelve zodiac signs serve as stations for the planets, mark the seasons, and order the inhabitants' livelihoods.
rows.anchor: وهي اثنا عشر برجا , هي للكواكب السيارة كالمنازل لأهلها , سميت بذلك لظهورها , وبنى عليها أمر الأرض

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the word for lamp in the plural, signaling a luminary magnificence greater than thousands of lamps.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بصسغة الجمع للتنبيه على عظمته في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun's course and the moon's movement complete the ordering of the cosmos, whose precise design makes doubt about its Creator or mercy irrational.
rows.anchor: أتم - بتنقلها فيها وبغير ذلك من أحوالهما - التدبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse says when, not if, because this response to ignorant people is habitual; it omits a repeated relative because walking humbly and answering gently form one trait of humility.
rows.anchor: دون ( إن ) لقضاء العادة بتحقق مدخولها , ولم يقل : والذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their address can come from ignorance or otherwise, at any time; the ignorant act against knowledge and wisdom.
rows.anchor: خطابا ما , بجهل أو غيره وفي وقت ما { الجاهلون } أي الذين يفعلون

rows.speaker: سيبويه عن أبي الخطاب
rows.claim: The reply means a peaceful disengagement, not a greeting, since Muslims had not yet been ordered to greet polytheists in this Meccan verse.
rows.anchor: نقل ذلك سيبويه عن أبي الخطاب , قال : لأن الآية فيما زعم مكية , ولم يؤمر المسلمون يومئذ أن يسلموا على المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No abrogation by the fighting verse is needed: turning away from fools and not retaliating is good manners under religion, protects one's honor, and is scrupulous.
rows.anchor: فلا حاجة إلى ادعاء نسخها بآية القتال ولا غيرها , لأن الإعضاء عن السفهاء وترك المقابلة مستحسن في الأدب والمروءة والشريعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is generalized because most ignorant speech is itself ignorance.
rows.anchor: وكأنه أطلق الخطاب إعلاما بأن أكثر قول الجاهل الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night overtakes a person whether asleep or awake, in contrast with daytime; the verse shifts from their dealings with people to private worship of their Creator.
rows.anchor: من البيتوتية : أن يدرك الليل نمت أو لم تنم , وهي خلاف الظلول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “for their Lord” indicates exclusivity: they enliven the night out of mercy for themselves and gratitude for His favor.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليهم برحمانيته , يحيون الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration is named first because it is prayer's most humbling, difficult pillar; standing after it confirms that both terms describe prayer.
rows.anchor: ولما كان السجود أشد أركان الصلاة تقريبا إلى الله , لكونه أنهى الخضوع

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says their day is marked by reverence and their night by submission.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحسن رحمه الله : نهارهم في خشوع , وليلهم في خضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fear shows they are not self-admiring; belief in the afterlife, denied by the ignorant, motivates their worship.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى أنه لا إعجاب عندهم , بل هم وجلون , وأن الحامل لهم على ذلك الإيمان باخرة التي كذب بها الجاهلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask first for rescue from Hell because they see themselves as deserving it despite striving, unable to give God His due measure.
rows.anchor: وقدموا الدعاء بالنجاة اهتماما بدرء المفسدة , وإشعارا بأنهم مستحقون لذلك وإن اجتهدوا , لتقصيرهم عن أن يقدروه سبحانه حق قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their description of Hell's torment as gharam means encompassing, persistent ruin and loss that humiliates whoever it binds.
rows.anchor: أي هلاكا وخسرانا ملحا محيطا بمن تعلق به مذلا له , دائما بمن غرى به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire is evil in every harmful aspect, both as a place of settlement and as a place of residence.
rows.anchor: أي تناهت هي في كل ما يحصل منه سوء , وهي في معنى بئست في جميع المذام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea rests on their return to God, as in the description of believers who act while their hearts tremble.
rows.anchor: إنهم إلى ربهم راجعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's emphatic assurance rules out what Moses feared; that protection means they can face Pharaoh directly despite his great realm and army.
rows.anchor: على هذا الوجه المؤكد , وكان ظهور ذلك في مقارعة الرأس أدل وأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “messenger” refers to both envoys as one collective: their mutual support and agreement make them like one soul.
rows.anchor: أفرده مريدا به الجنس الصالح للاثنين , إشارة بالتوحيد إلى أنهما في تعاضدهما واتفاقهما كالنفس الواحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either the wording could occur twice in separate forms or once with an understood dual sense; a singular expression suits this context better than the wording in Taha, which stresses a request for support.
rows.anchor: أو مرة بما يفيد التثنية والاتفاق , فساغ التعبير بكل منهما , ولم يثن هنا لأن المقام لا اقتضاء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Send the Children of Israel with us” means release the people enslaved unjustly, who have no rightful claim over them, so they may go to the holy land promised through their prophetic ancestors.
rows.anchor: أي خل وأطلق ؛ وأعاد الضمير على معنى رسول فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account consoles Muhammad by paralleling mockery of Moses with other attacks on the Prophet and confirms the divine promise to protect him.
rows.anchor: تسلية لهذا النبي الكريم وتحقيقا لمعنى قوله تعالى { كلا } و { مستمعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh directs the reply to Moses because he regards him as the principal messenger and Aaron as only his minister.
rows.anchor: مخاطبا لموسى عليه السلام علما منه أنه الأصل فيها , وأخوه إنما هو وزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh presents himself as the powerful guardian who raised Moses from infancy, implying that this past care should restrain Moses from confronting him.
rows.anchor: اي بعظمتنا التي شاهدتها { فينا وليدا } أي صغيرا قريب عهد بالولادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “You lived among us” means Moses was not elsewhere but belonged to Pharaoh's household and appeared honored by them.
rows.anchor: اي لا في غيرنا , باعتبار انقطاعك إلينا , وتعززك في الظاهر بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's phrasing suggests a long, bitter stay: his fear came true and his precautions failed to prevent the killing of Israelite children.
rows.anchor: اي كثير , فلنا عليك بذلك من ا لحق ما ينبغي أن يمنعك من مواجهتنا بمثل هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means Moses killed an Egyptian Copt, then claims that doing so makes him ungrateful for royal upbringing and for the king's favor.
rows.anchor: أي من قتل القطبي , ثم أكد نسبته إلى ذلك مشيرا غلى أنه عامله بالحلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh counts the victim as one of his own and treats Moses's earlier silence about Israel as proof that he belonged to Pharaoh's people before prophethood.
rows.anchor: بقتل من ينسب إلي , أو عده منهم لسكوته عنهم إذا ذاك , لأنه لم يكن قبل الرسالة مأمورا فيهم بشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers in a reversed order, acknowledging the killing first; al-Tabari says Arabs use “misguidance” for ignorance and ignorance for misguidance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : والعرب تضع الضلال موضع الجهل والجهل موضع الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses explains that he acted while unguided in religion, waiting for God to direct him; his killing of the man was an accident.
rows.anchor: أي لا أعرف دينا , فأنا واقف عن كل وجهة حتى يوجهني ربي إلى ما يشاء

rows.speaker: ابن جرير
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reports that Arabic usage can put “misguidance” in place of ignorance and ignorance in place of misguidance.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جرير : والعرب تضع الضلال موضع الجهل والجهل موضع الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses fled Pharaoh's force and the people who would incite him, fearing execution for the killing, though the deed was accidental and the victim's blood was legally permissible.
rows.anchor: على نفسي أن تقتلوني بذلك القتيل الذي قتلته خطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave Moses wisdom, practical knowledge fit for wise judges, and made him a messenger; he now fears neither death nor anything else from Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: اي علما أعمل به عمل الحكام الحكماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Pharaoh combined reproach and boasting, Moses answers the reproach first as the later and more immediate point, then turns to the supposed favor.
rows.anchor: ولما اجتمع في كلام فرعون من وتعيير , بدأ بجوابه عن التعيير لأنه الأخير فكان أقرب , ولأنه أهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's phrasing asks the question without an explicit particle of denial, keeping the rebuke concise and courteous.
rows.anchor: فقال موبخا له مبكتا منكرا عليه غير أنه حذف حرف الإنكار إجمالا في القول وإحسانا في الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recasts Pharaoh's supposed favor as the very enslavement of Israel, replacing the claimed favor with the injustice that cancels it.
rows.anchor: جعله نفسها فقال مبدلا منها تنبيها على إحباطها , وإعلاما بأنها - بكونها نقمة - أولى منها في عدها نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel descends from prophets, and Joseph had saved Egyptians' lives and freed them; Pharaoh's later enslavement and killing of sons led to Moses's arrival in his household.
rows.anchor: وهو أبناء الأنبياء , ولسلفهم يوسف عليه السلام عليكم من المنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh turns from Moses's rebuke because it exposed God's complete power and knowledge in the events of Moses's life, and shifts to the mission to mislead his people.
rows.anchor: فهم ما في جوابه هذا الأخير من الذم له والتعجيز , وإثبات القدرة التامة والعلم الشامل لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's question about the Lord's nature is really denial and feigned ignorance, though he knew God's acts, as Moses later says in al-Israʾ.
rows.anchor: منكرا لخالقه على سبيل التجاهل , كما أنكر هؤلاء الرحمن متجاهلين وهو أعرف الناس بغالب أفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses avoids defining God's essence, which cannot be described by itself, and identifies Him through His clearest necessary acts, establishing that He has no peer.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تعريف حقيقته سبحانه بنفسها محالا لعدم التركيب , فكان تعريفها لا يصح إلا بالخارج اللازم الجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord” means creator, originator, and governor of the heavens, earth, and everything between; all people depend on Him, unlike Pharaoh's supposed benefaction.
rows.anchor: أي خالق ومبدع ومدبر { السماوات } كلها { والأرض } وإت تباعدت أجرامها بعضها عن بعض { وما بينهما }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the listeners are firmly certain, they will recognize that a changing created world has an unchanging changer, the God who sent Moses.
rows.anchor: إن كنتم } اي كونا راسخا { موقنين * } أي متصفين بما عليه أهل العلم بأصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh asks his nearby courtiers whether they hear Moses, appearing to object that Moses answered with acts instead of the essence; he could use this as subtle deceit if challenged.
rows.anchor: وهو كلام ظاهرة أنه نبههم عن الإنكار , لأنه سأل عن الماهية , فأجيب بغيرها , ويحتمل غير ذلك لو ضويق فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the universal proof, Moses specifies the Lord of Pharaoh and their earliest ancestors, whose observed coming-to-be prevents any claim that they are lords.
rows.anchor: مخصصا بعد ما عمم بشيء لا تمكن المنازعة فيه لمشاهدة وجود أفراده بعد أن لم تكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh was then either sheer nonexistence or only fluid in his father's back; their ancestors too had perished, so none could be lord of later generations.
rows.anchor: وفرعون - الذي تقرون بأنه ربكم - كان إذ ذاك عدما محضا , أو ماء صرفا في ظهر أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh sarcastically calls Moses “your messenger” and repeats “sent to you” to ridicule the claim that a messenger should be sane enough to understand his question.
rows.anchor: على طريق التهكم , إشارة إلى أن الرسول ينبغي ان يكون أعقل الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord of east and west governs the rising and setting and their times and places, as well as all people, animals, and inanimate things between them.
rows.anchor: اي الشروق والغروب ووقتهما وموضعهما { وما بينهما } اي من الناس الذين ليسوا في طاعتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated movement of sun, moon, and stars orders day and night and human affairs; without it people could not know or manage their lives.
rows.anchor: بسبب ما ترون من قدرته على تقليب النيرات من بزوغ الشمس والقمر والنجوم وأفولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is the clearest proof because the motion recurs; Abraham used the same argument to stun Nimrod.
rows.anchor: وهذا الدليل أبين الكل لتكرر الحركة فيه وغير ذلك من معالمه , ولذلك بهت نمرود لما ألقاه عليه الخليل عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reasoning from the signs means recognizing God; this leaves Pharaoh's audience to choose whether Moses is mad or they are rational, in answer to their unsupported accusation.
rows.anchor: بما أشار إليه من الأدلة في مقابلة ما نسبوه إليه من الجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses's answer wounds more yet remains gentle, and makes the truth clearer while preserving dignity as it seeks to rescue them from error.
rows.anchor: فكان قوله أنكأ مع أنه ألطف , وأوضح مع أنه أستر وأشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After being silenced, Pharaoh abandons argument for coercion, threatening imprisonment; the shift to force shows his defeat.
rows.anchor: عادلا عن الحجاج بعد الخوض فيه إلى المغالبة التي هي أبين علامات الانقطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks patiently whether Pharaoh would imprison him even if he brought a clear sign, seeking to give every person a fair chance to believe.
rows.anchor: مدافعا بالتي هي أحسن إرخاء للعنان , لإرادة البيان , حتى لا يبقى عذر لإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fairness normally invites people to return to truth and acknowledge it, so Moses hopes Pharaoh will leave tyranny for faith.
rows.anchor: لأن من العادة الجارية السكون إلى الإنصاف , والرجوع إلى الحق والاعتراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh says “bring it” hoping to find grounds for denial or confusion; asking if Moses is truthful implies miracles verify true messengers because God does not validate liars.
rows.anchor: طمعا في أن يجد موضعا للتكذيب أو التلبيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff became a plainly manifest serpent, unlike the illusions and imitations produced by magic.
rows.anchor: اي حية في غاية الكبر { مبين * } أي ظاهر الثعبانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hand had been burned by a coal when Moses was in Pharaoh's lap; Pharaoh's doctors had failed to cure it, and Moses now draws it from his pocket.
rows.anchor: التي كانت احترقت لما أخذ الجمرة وهو في حجر فرعون , وبذل فرعون جهده في علاجها بجميع من قدر عليه من الأطباء فعجز عن إبرائها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its whiteness shone with extraordinary brightness like the sun and nearly overwhelmed the eyes of its viewers.
rows.anchor: بياضا تتوفر الدواعي على نظره لخروجه عن العادة بأن له نورا كنور الشمس يكاد يغشي الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account assigns the sorcery accusation specifically to Pharaoh because he dominates the narrative and his submission would entail his followers' submission; it does not exclude their saying it in deference, as in al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: خص في هذه السورة إسنادا هذا الكلام إليه لأن السياق كله لتخصيصه الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Abraham narrative follows Moses to show divine mercy, console the Prophet over the denials and taunts in al-Furqan, and highlight Abraham's distinctive challenge to his father and people over idols.
rows.anchor: أتبعه دلاله على رحيميته قصة إبراهيم عليه السلام لما تقدم أنه شاركه فيه مما يسلي عما وقع ذكره عنهم من التعنتات في الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Abraham is a great ancestor of Arabs, his example can lead them to monotheism despite their imitation of tradition and curb their reverence for idolatrous ancestors.
rows.anchor: وهو أعظم آباء العرب , ليكون ذلك حاملا لهم على تقليده في التوحيد إن كانوا لا ينفكون عن التقليد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Recite” means connected, repeated reading; the wording supports taking “when” as “remember,” and its changed phrasing draws Arabs' attention to their special tie to Abraham.
rows.anchor: اي قرأ قراءة متتابعة - مرجح للتقدير الأول في { وإذ } من جعله ( اذكر )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The audience consists of people deceived by idols and denying human messengers; Abraham's story is a great report about his address to his father and people.
rows.anchor: اي على هؤلاء المغترين بالأوثان , النكرين لرسالة البشر { نبأ إبراهيم * } أي خبره العظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham already knew what his people worshiped; he asks to draw their attention to its ugliness, using the present tense to picture their habitual practice.
rows.anchor: منبها لهم على ضلالهم , لا مستعلما لأنه كان عالما بحقيقة حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters boast at length that they worship idols and persist in devotion, portraying their worship as a proud achievement.
rows.anchor: مبتهجين بسؤاله , مظهرين الافتخار في جوابهم بإطالة الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We remain devoted” presents persistence as the result of worship; they crowd around the idols and confine themselves to their service.
rows.anchor: أنا نوفي حق العبادة بأن ندوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verb usually indicates daytime duration, they may mean continued devotion all the more at night; it is also used without a daytime restriction elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي أوجب تفسير الظلول بمطلق الدوام وإن كان معناه الدوام بقيد النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prolonged answer exposes blind imitation born of ignorance about worship and false confidence that they have gained something great.
rows.anchor: فجروا على منوال هؤلاء في داء التقليد الناشىء عن الجهل بنفس العبادة وبظنهم مع ذلك أنهم على طائل كبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's father and people persisted in misguidance and were destined for the Fire; he could only call them, an occasion for sorrow and consolation to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وزاد قوم إبراهيم عليه السلام أن استمروا على ضلالهم وأبوه معهم فكانوا حطب النار , ولم يتكمن من إنقاذهم من ذلك
